output_cells.text: (ii) Do the national rules regarding form/content of communications with clients derive from, and are they broadly in line with, MiFID II or are there additional national requirements?  Please also confirm that EEA OFIs which have no licensed office in your jurisdiction (i.e. who are providing cross-border services, rather than services from an establishment in your jurisdiction) will not be required to comply with content requirements deriving from MiFID II as implemented in your jurisdiction but rather the equivalent requirements of its home EEA member state.

Funds & IMAS  Yes, for communications to Professional Investors, the key requirement is that the communication is "fair, clear and not misleading". The form/content requirements for communications to Retail Investors are considerably more onerous. However, the Liechtenstein rules regarding form/content of communications with clients are broadly in line with MiFID II; however in relation to Retail Investors additional Liechtenstein laws are applicable, such as the long distance distribution legislation for financial services. For more information, please refer to section 10 of the European Framework Document and seek local law advice on a case-by-case basis.  OFIs which have no office or branch in Liechtenstein would be considered to be providing cross-border services and would basically be required to comply with content requirements under the law of their home EEA Member State and, in relation to Retail Investors, to the above-mentioned Liechtenstein provisions. However, please note that exceptions may apply in relation to local due diligence/KYC laws which may also be relevant for such EEA OFIs. It is recommendable to seek specific legal advice to check whether an EEA OFI would be required to comply with such local laws.  Funds only:  Yes, such rules are included in the AIFMG and in the UCITSG, as further detailed in sections 6.1 and 6.2 above.  Note that, where marketing to Retail Investors, it is necessary to include information in written marketing materials on where the prospectus, KID and annual report can be obtained.  ESMA's Guidelines on Funds Marketing Communications  The FMA is expected to comply with ESMA's guidelines on marketing communications under the Regulation on cross-border distribution of funds, published on the 2 August 2021. These guidelines, applied from 2 February 2022, and as amended from time to time, and specify the application of the requirements for marketing communications set out in Article 4(1) of the Regulation (EU) 2019/1156 of 20 June 2019 by establishing common principles on the following matters, while taking into account online aspects of such marketing communications: - the identification as such of marketing communications (the guideline proposes for example a particular disclaimer in this respect); - the description of risks and rewards in an equally prominent manner, which is substantially aligned with existing provisions in French law; and - the fair, clear and not misleading character of marketing communications (General requirements, Information on risks and rewards as well as costs, past performance and expected future performance and information on sustainability-related aspects).  These Marketing Guidelines apply to all marketing communications addressed to investors or potential investors in UCITS and AIFs (including those set up as EuVECAs, EuSEFs, ELTIFs and money market funds). In absence of a definition of what constitutes a "marketing communication" the Marketing Guidelines instead provide non-exhaustive examples of what may and may not qualify. There is no explicit published guidance on this question but counsel strongly recommends that a non-EEA AIFM marketing an AIF in Liechtenstein also complies with these Guidelines.  Notably all mediums, including paper printed documents or information made available in electronic format, interviews, advertisements, documents made available on the internet, as well as webpages (including messages broadcast on any social media platform), video presentations, live presentations, radio messages or factsheets are within scope.
